name: Illuminating Emerald
lede: Illuminating Emerald is a deep, metallic bluish-green named as a variant of [[emerald]], sold by Crayola as one of its Metallic FX crayons.

sections.title: A metallic variant of emerald
sections.body:
The parent word is emerald, the green gem whose name traces through Old French *esmeralde* to the Greek *smaragdos*, meaning simply "green gemstone" [1]. "Illuminating" is the modifier: Crayola released this shade in 2001 as part of its Metallic FX line, sixteen crayons with a metallic finish whose names were chosen through a contest open to residents of the United States and Canada [2]. It reads darker and more blue-shifted than Crayola's plain Emerald crayon [2].

The nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[dark-sulphate-green]], with [[paolo-veronese-green]] close by, more vivid [3]. [[scarab]], [[ocean-green]] and [[viridian]] sit further out in the same general family [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for this green in 10 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.04 percent, rarer than 79 percent of the named colors we track, as photographed [4]. The earliest match is dated 1827, in a work by T. Davies; the third-earliest is 1893 and the latest 1940, across 8 dated paintings [4]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so that is a floor, not a first, and as a named crayon the color itself did not exist before 2001 [2][4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors matched to the swatch, not identifications of any actual metallic pigment [4].

origin.named_after: emerald (the gemstone), with the modifier "Illuminating" from Crayola's Metallic FX naming contest

questions.answer: A contest open to U.S. and Canada residents

openers: Illuminating Emerald is a 2001 Crayola metallic crayon, so no painting before that year could use it by that name.

issues: Crayola naming-contest attribution is for the Metallic FX set, not confirmed for this specific name
